{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Kubient / Customer "AP")

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Subject:** Playbook review of Exhibit 10.14 Master Services Agreement, dated 5 February  
**Scope:** 18 playbook rules assessed against the executed form; findings below are limited to verified review output.

---

## 1. Executive summary

The Agreement is, on balance, favourable to us on the commercial-restraint rules: there is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no liquidated damages payable by us, and no audit or non-solicitation right running against us. Section 1 affirmatively confirms we remain free to offer Inventory through other agents or sell to third parties. The Vendor indemnity in §10(a) is broad and sits at or above our preferred position, with indemnification carved out of the consequential-damages waiver in §7(a) and no super-cap. Governing law (Delaware, New York courts) sits at our fallback.

Five items require action. Two are critical: (i) **there is no monetary liability cap anywhere in the document** — §7 is a bare mutual consequential-damages waiver, leaving direct liability unlimited in both directions and failing even the fallback; and (ii) **there is no IP or data ownership provision at all**, so nothing allocates ownership of our Content, Properties, Requests or the visitor data Kubient collects and stores under §9(b)(iii). In addition, the Auction Platform licence is expressly **revocable** with no qualification and excludes our affiliates and contractors (with §8(a) barring third-party access), the auto-renewal has **no non-renewal mechanic** (effective 90-day opt-out only), there is **no transition assistance or data-return obligation** (§4(c) permits Kubient to elect destruction), and there is **no insurance obligation** on a vendor that processes visitor data.

Three findings (Termination for Convenience, Audit, Non-solicitation) are recorded as `needs_review` because deterministic keyword checks failed on phrasing or on the absence of a clause to measure; on substantive re-review each was assessed as compliant, but each should be confirmed before we sign off. The Warranty finding was repaired in review and is compliant at or above the preferred position.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | Preamble (§7) | No monetary cap anywhere; document-wide search for "exceed"/"aggregate" returns none. Unlimited direct liability fails the fallback (mutual 12-month cap). Carve-out architecture (indemnity, confidentiality) is acceptable and mutual. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Missing** | Preamble (§14(b), §6(a), §9(b)) | No IP/data ownership provision. §14(b) covers only names, marks and logos; §9(b)(i)/(viii) confirm Kubient owns the Service and "products delivered hereunder" with no assignment or licence-back to us. No assignment of our IP to Kubient, so not walk-away, but neither preferred nor fallback is met. |
| 3 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Preamble (§10(a), §11, §7(a)) | Broad defend/indemnify/hold-harmless covering the Services, Auction Platform, Creative, breach of warranty and acts/omissions of Kubient and subcontractors; §9(b)(i) non-infringement, §9(b)(iii) data security and §9(b)(v)/(ix) compliance heads all captured, no infringement carve-outs. At or above preferred. |
| 4 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | Preamble (¶2, ¶8(a), ¶4(c)(ii), ¶14(h)) | Grant is expressly "revocable" without qualification (¶4(c)(ii) confirms revocation on termination but does not limit it to that event), names only Customer, and ¶8(a) bars third-party access absent Kubient consent — the rule's walk-away case. Transfer prong largely met via ¶14(h). |
| 5 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | Preamble (§(h), §2) | Mutual right to assign without consent to affiliates, asset purchasers and merger/stock-sale successors; other assignments on consent not unreasonably withheld — our fallback structure with the M&A carve-out present. No change-of-control clause anywhere. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble (§1) | Exclusivity expressly disclaimed; we remain free to use other agents or sell to third parties. Other "exclusive" hits are jurisdiction, marks ownership, entire agreement and no-third-party-beneficiary. Preferred position. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Preamble (§1) | No non-compete, field-of-use or territory restriction; only "shall not" covenants relate to Creative/content standards and prohibited ad categories. Preferred position; benefits us. |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | Preamble (§4(a), §5, §7(a)) | No LDs, penalty, early-termination fee or minimum-fee-on-termination on us. §4(a) entitles Kubient only to revenue share actually generated during the 90-day notice period. §7(a) mutually excludes punitive damages. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review** (assessed compliant at fallback) | Preamble (¶4(a), §5) | Right to terminate "for any reason" after the 1-year Initial Term on 90 days' notice — a convenience right; the deterministic check searched for literal "for convenience". 1-year term with 1-year renewals, no early-termination fee, mid-term bar is symmetric. No refund issue as §5 is a revenue share paying us. |
| 10 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal window | **Deviation** | Preamble (¶4(a)) | Automatic 1-year renewals with no non-renewal mechanic; only exit is 90 days' convenience notice, so the effective opt-out is 90 days — fails the 60-day fallback and sits at the edge of walk-away. Renewal length acceptable; no uplift risk (revenue share). |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | Preamble (¶4(c)) | ¶4(c) covers only cessation of Services, licence revocation, and return **or destruction** of Confidential Information. No transition assistance, no usable-format data return, no deletion certification. Kubient may unilaterally destroy our data — walk-away territory. |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Needs review** (assessed compliant) | Preamble (§1, §5) | No audit, inspection or records right over us anywhere (p0000–p0074). §1 access/cooperation covenant is service-enablement only, with no system-access grant. Absence is better than preferred; the failed frequency check reflects the absence of any clause to measure. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Needs review** (assessed compliant) | Preamble (§14 misc. provisions) | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant; miscellaneous provisions contain none. Preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer). Failed duration/carve-out sub-checks are artifacts of absence. |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | Preamble (§14(a), §8) | Delaware law (accepted list, at fallback) with exclusive jurisdiction and venue in New York state and federal courts. Noted: §8 AAA Commercial Arbitration sits in tension with exclusive court jurisdiction; domestic, so no walk-away trigger. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | Preamble (§1, §5) | No MFN or price/terms-matching provision in either direction. Preferred position; non-exclusivity in §1 reinforces our freedom to deal on any terms. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments/volume restrictions | Compliant | Preamble (§1, §5) | No minimum purchase, take-or-pay or volume commitment; Services engaged per Exhibit on a specific-engagement basis, with revenue share paid to us within 7 days of receipt. Winning Bid Price floor is set by us, not a commitment. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant (repaired) | Preamble (§9(b), §13) | Live express warranties: material performance to industry standards, freedom from errors materially affecting utility, no malicious code, compliance with Laws throughout the Term. §13 disclaimer is double-carved and reaches implied warranties only. Term-long duration exceeds preferred parameters. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Preamble (§14) | No insurance obligation on either Party and no Exhibit reference to coverage, despite Kubient hosting the Auction Platform and warranting at §9(b)(iii) that it collects, manages and stores visitor data. Walk-away territory under the rule. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following were identified in review as walk-away positions or at their edge, and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **Licence revocable at will, affiliates and contractors excluded (¶2 with ¶8(a))** — the combination of unqualified revocability and exclusion of affiliates/contractors with no path to add them is expressly the rule's walk-away case and fails the fallback, which requires affiliate coverage on notice at minimum.
2. **Unilateral destruction of our data on termination (¶4(c))** — the "return or destroy" election permits Kubient to destroy our data; combined with the absence of any transition assistance or export right, this fails the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export) and is walk-away territory.
3. **No vendor insurance of any kind (§14)** — a vendor that processes personal/visitor data with no insurance at all is walk-away territory under the rule.
4. **Auto-renewal with a 90-day effective opt-out and no non-renewal mechanic (¶4(a))** — fails the 60-day fallback and sits at the edge of walk-away.
5. **No liability cap (§7)** — not characterised as walk-away, but flagged critical: unlimited direct liability fails the core material term of the fallback and must be resolved.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Serve the five substantive redlines**, in priority order:
   - **§7** — insert a mutual monetary cap with uncapped Excluded Claims. Because §5 is a revenue share under which Kubient pays us, a cap keyed only to "fees paid by Customer" would be illusory; use amounts **paid or payable between the parties** plus the USD 1,000,000 floor from the preferred position, and expressly keep §5 revenue-share amounts outside the cap.
   - **New ownership clause** — we retain all rights in our Content, Properties and data; Kubient keeps its platform and background IP; deliverables assigned with a licence-back to embedded Kubient IP; joint ownership excluded.
   - **¶2 licence grant** — extend to our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (we remain responsible for their compliance), limit revocation to expiration or termination under ¶4, and conform transferability to ¶14(h).
   - **¶4(c)** — insert transition assistance, machine-readable return of Customer Data within 30 days, and certified deletion.
   - **¶4(a)** — add a 30-day Customer non-renewal right, leaving the existing 90-day mutual convenience right untouched; 60 days is an acceptable fallback.
2. **Insert the insurance paragraph as new §14(j)** at preferred limits (CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate; E&O USD 2M; cyber USD 5M where Kubient processes our or visitor data; workers' compensation as required by Law; certificates on request), offering the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) in the comment. One paragraph, no other terms disturbed.
3. **Close out the three `needs_review` findings** (T4C, Audit, Non-solicitation) internally. Each failed only a deterministic keyword or sub-element check — phrasing variance in the case of T4C ("for any reason" rather than "for convenience"), and absence of a clause to measure in the case of Audit and Non-solicitation. Confirm and record as compliant; no counterparty-facing comment.
4. **Raise two clean-up points** without treating them as deviations: the tension between §14(a) exclusive court jurisdiction and §8 AAA arbitration, and the breadth of our reciprocal indemnity at §10(b) (which reaches our breach of any representation or warranty and our acts or omissions rather than being confined to Content/Properties and breach of law) — better addressed under the customer-indemnity rule than by reopening §10(a).
5. **Diligence the Exhibits.** Exhibits are incorporated under §1. Any Exhibit or later amendment should be checked for minimum volume or spend language and for audit or system-access rights; if audit language appears, we will require the preferred parameters (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access).
"}
